arw_through_the_wall.description: Thoradin's Wall closes the south-east corner of Hillsbrad, and it's been shut for as long as anyone at Tarren Mill has been posted here. On a clear day I can see the gap in it from the air, and the gap is open. The commander won't send a column through a gap she knows nothing about, and she won't let me fly a wyvern over it either, so she's sending one person, and that's you. Get through the gap and keep going until you find whoever holds the other side. Then come back and tell me whether they're holding it against us.
arw_through_the_wall.accept_text: It's south-east of Tarren Mill, at the far end of the valley, past Durnholde and the ogres' stead.
arw_through_the_wall.turn_in_text:
There's a Horde camp, in a human ruin, flying our colours and using the ruin's own name for itself.

That's better than what I expected. Go back and tell their commander the wall works both ways now.

arw_what_killed_the_scout.description: I've got a body and no answer. One of Scout Halm's runners went north to look at the wall and came back over a horse, and the wounds on him are from an animal I can't name. There are four punctures in an arc, and the arc's wider than a wolf's. The moor people up past the wall call them highland fleshrippers, and whatever did this is standing on that moor right now, being perfectly ordinary to everyone who lives there. I've a professional objection to not being able to name things, so kill a few and bring me their dewclaws.
arw_what_killed_the_scout.accept_text: I want to see whether the spacing's consistent, or whether I'm looking at one very large animal.
arw_what_killed_the_scout.turn_in_text:
It's consistent, so it's a species and not a monster, which is the better of the two answers, and the one that means there are a great many of them.

I'll write it up as a highland fleshripper. Somebody has probably named it already, and I don't care.

hbe_bandits.description: The Syndicate have stopped robbing the eastern roads and started owning them. I don't much mind robbery, because robbery is weather. What I mind is that the same three bends have been manned at the same hours for a fortnight, and bandits don't keep hours like that. A toll does, and a toll means administration. Clear them off the eastern roads, and look at what they're wearing, violet sashes in Alterac's colour, kept long after there's a kingdom to wear it for.
hbe_bandits.accept_text: Take the sashes if you want my thanks in writing. Nothing else they carry has a maker's mark.

hbe_consignment.description: I run the carts, flour west out of Tarren Mill and reagents back east, twice a month without fail for six years. The last two runs west didn't arrive. The Syndicate have learned what a cart looks like, so I'd like to try something that doesn't look like one. Here are four sacks, sealed with my mark, and they go on your back instead of on an axle. Take the west road all the way to the forward post in the fields and ask for Quartermaster Ivek, who's expecting a cart and will be delighted.
hbe_consignment.accept_text: Don't set it down, not to rest, not to fight. A seal that's touched the ground is one somebody can swear was opened.

hbe_ditch_samples.description: I sample the ditches east of the mill so the apothecaries inside the walls don't have to. For a month they've been running with something that isn't runoff, and the stretch where it's worst lies uphill of the vats. That rules out the one explanation everybody had ready, and yes, I know what we do here, which is exactly why I want to be certain it isn't us. I don't want jars of ditchwater, I can fill those myself. Take the samples off the worgs that drink there, because a creature that's drunk it for a month is a better record than anything I could dip.
hbe_ditch_samples.accept_text: If it's us, I'd rather find it than have a farmer find it. Bring me what's in their coats.
hbe_ditch_samples.turn_in_text:
They're all uphill, and the worst of them a half mile above the vats.

So it isn't us. That means I've got to go and tell the Society that something else is in this water, and they're going to be very disappointed in me for being right.

hbe_durnholde_watch.description: Durnholde Keep has been held by the Syndicate for longer than it was ever held by Lordaeron, and I'd like that said out loud more often than it is. Its watchmen patrol the bluff outside the walls in Durnholde grey plate with Syndicate violet painted over it. They haven't forged a breastplate in fifteen years. They're wearing a dead kingdom's kit with a dead kingdom's colours brushed on top, and the paint's worn through at the shoulders. Thin them out on the bluff, and scratch the paint on one before you come back.
hbe_durnholde_watch.accept_text: Scratch it right down. I want you to see the grey for yourself.
hbe_durnholde_watch.turn_in_text:
It's grey underneath, I know. I've known for two years.

I keep sending people up there, half hoping somebody will come back and tell me I'm wrong about it.

hbe_fissure_north.description: Gavin's Naze is the Alterac road and the Syndicate's front door, and I know every track off it. Three years ago a fissure opened in the foothills north of the Naze, in ground three kingdoms had surveyed without finding anything. Blood elves have used it as a supply road most of that time, and the Syndicate sit on the north track watching them come and go and taking a tithe. Clear the Syndicate off that track, then go up to the mouth and look down it. I've had two men offer to go in, and I've told both of them no.
hbe_fissure_north.accept_text: Look down it, and don't go in. Not until somebody can tell me what's at the bottom.

hbe_gavin.description: Everything stolen in this valley passes through Gavin's hands, and Gavin keeps a ledger of names, dates, and what was paid. I don't particularly want him dead. I want the ledger, and he's made it clear those are the same errand. He's in the centre of the camp at Gavin's Naze, east of the mill. The ledger will be on him, because he's never once let it out of reach, which is the single most useful thing about him.
hbe_gavin.accept_text: Everything he owns opens without a sound, the ground under his tent included. If he vanishes, don't assume he's run.

hbe_gnolls.description: I've run a trapline in Mudsnout Hollow for eleven years. Last month the gnolls took the whole of it, snares, wire, bait, the lot, and left the stakes standing in the ground in a neat row. They didn't miss them. They pulled the line, coiled the wire, and left me the bits I'd have to dig out, and scavengers don't do that. I've chosen to take it personally. Go into the hollow proper and thin them out.
hbe_gnolls.accept_text: They den in the low wet ground. Go in from the high side and let them come up to you.
hbe_gnolls.turn_in_text:
That's done it.

I've been doing this eleven years, and I've never once been mocked by the wildlife. I'd like it on record that I'm handling it well.

hbe_gorbash.description: Da ogres have a leader, and at some point he took da stead's own millstone off its spindle to use as a thrown weapon. I watched him do it, wit my own eyes, more dan once. I know how dat sounds. I said it four times now, and every time da face is da same. He is in da barn, and he throws da millstone.
hbe_gorbash.accept_text: Watch his shoulders. Dey drop before he lifts, and dat is all da warning anyone gets.
hbe_gorbash.turn_in_text:
Da millstone is back on its spindle. It took four of us to lift what he was throwing wit one hand.

Nobody is going to believe dis report. I stopped caring.

hbe_grik.description: A gnoll pack is weather, but a gnoll pack with a chief is politics, and politics is my department. Grik has taken the Mudsnout from a nuisance that raids barns to a force that picks which barns, and in which order. He carries a cleaver with a notch filed in it for every farmstead between the hollow and the road, and I'm told he adds them himself, afterwards, in front of the pack. He's deep in the hollow, at the den mouth. Count the notches when he's down, because I need the number for the ledger and I don't want it secondhand.
hbe_grik.accept_text: Count them once, carefully. I'll only want to hear the number one time.
hbe_grik.turn_in_text:
How many was it? Say it once more, and then we'll neither of us repeat it.

I'll enter it in the ledger, and I'll make sure the ledger is somewhere the farm families never find it.

hbe_impossible_yetis.description: I've given eleven years to Alterac yeti, and I'm the authority on them, largely because nobody competed for the position. A caravan master came through Tarren Mill with a story about yeti on the far side of the world, in a desert province of Kalimdor, and I haven't been able to put it down. Yeti don't cross oceans, they don't cross rivers, and the caravan master was extremely sure. I'm not asking you to believe it. Carry this across an ocean, put it in the hand of whoever's senior at that logging camp, and let them tell me I've wasted everyone's time.
hbe_impossible_yetis.accept_text: It's sealed, so don't open it. The questions inside are embarrassing, and I'd like them answered before they're laughed at.
hbe_impossible_yetis.turn_in_text: She writes a very careful letter for a woman who's already made up her mind. Tell her yes. Tell her there are yeti in this mountain, that they didn't walk here, and that all of us would sleep better if her impossibility had held.

hbe_ironbeard.description: The road patrol has a sergeant, and I'm certain he's the reason ten riflemen volley instead of firing. Dwarven discipline is the only thing turning that picket into a problem, and discipline has a name and stands at the end of the line. Break him and the rest shoot like men who are frightened, which they are. They're a garrison a very long way from Dun Morogh, holding a ridge nobody in Ironforge has thought about in a decade. He's on the Dun Garok Road, south of the mill.
hbe_ironbeard.accept_text: He calls the volley, and you'll hear him before the first shot. Go for him when he does.
hbe_ironbeard.turn_in_text:
That hammer's dwarven make, and it shows in the balance. You can feel where they put the weight.

Keep it for yourself. I measure things. I've never once had cause to swing one.

hbe_ogres.description: Generations of Nethanders worked dat stead, and dey raised da barn in a single season wit dere own hands. Da ogres took da whole holding in an afternoon, and now dey are living in da barn. I got no love for human farms. But dey built dat barn in a season, and da ogres are using it as a privy, and taking a ting and ruining it, dey are different tings. Dey are round da stead, so go and thin dem out.
hbe_ogres.accept_text: Dey hit like a wall coming down. Keep moving, and never let dem put you against da fences.
hbe_ogres.turn_in_text:
Done, and dey are still in da barn.

But dere is more room in it now, and dey have started arguing about who sleeps where. Dat is how dis ends, and not wit us.

hbe_riflemen.description: The Stormpike cut a fort square into the southern ridge and put riflemen on the road beneath it. My orders are to find a way into that fort other than the front door, and it's hard to survey a road you keep being shot on. Here's the trick, and it cost me a hat to learn it. They sight for the length of the road and not one pace further, so get inside that and a rifle's an expensive club. Clear them off the south road for me.
hbe_riflemen.accept_text: The danger's the hundred yards before you're inside their sights. Cover that ground fast.

hbe_route_card.description: The card is oiled linen, folded small, and the Syndicate bandit you took it from had it sewn inside a cuff. One side is a sketch of the Alterac foothills with the fissure marked. The other is a list of times, arrivals and departures at the mouth, kept nightly, in a careful hand, for four months.
hbe_route_card.accept_text:
Somebody paid the Syndicate to count blood elves going into a hole in the ground, and the Syndicate did it properly for four months.

Bring me more tallies off their couriers on the Naze road. Whoever commissioned this wasn't after the elves. You don't need four months of arrivals to rob a column. You need four months of arrivals to work out what's down there and how much of it there is.
hbe_route_card.turn_in_text:
These tallies are in different hands, all from one ledger, and not one of those hands is Syndicate.

They were counting for somebody else. I do this work for a living, and I didn't know anyone else was doing it on my road.

hbe_shamans.description: The Mudsnout have shamans now, which they didn't have a year ago. I've watched them work from cover, and it isn't posturing. The weather follows them down the hollow, and the worgs follow the weather. A year ago they were dogs with knives, and something's taught them, quickly. I'd dearly like to know what a gnoll pack had to trade for lessons, but first I'd like the shamans gone.
hbe_shamans.accept_text: You'll hear the rattles long before you see them. Once you start, don't stop to think about it.

hbe_snares.description: The snares the gnolls took were made by hand, one at a time, over eleven winters. I'm realistic about how many will have survived a month in a gnoll den, and I'd like whatever's left. They hang them up in the dens, which is insulting, but at least it's tidy. The wire's what matters, because I can cut new stakes in an afternoon. Good wire comes up from Southshore twice a year if the road's open, and the road hasn't been open.
hbe_snares.accept_text: You'll find them in bunches, not scattered. Bring the whole bunch, tangles and all.

hbe_spellbinders.description: Gavin's Naze is a fence's camp with delusions of being a guild, and I've been inside it twice. The bandits don't trouble me. What troubles me is that the camp keeps spellbinders, and no fence anywhere needs one unless somebody else is paying to put him there. A trained binder could sell his talent in any city still standing, and instead he's stood in a scrap camp in the Hillsbrad hills. They hold the inner ring of the camp, south-east of the mill. Clear them out, and let's see who notices.
hbe_spellbinders.accept_text: They bind you in place before they do anything else. Go in fast, and go in with someone.

hbe_stillwater.description: The Syndicate keep a warden on Durnholde's outer ground. He wears a keep guard's greatsword and a keep guard's rank, both taken off the men who held the place before him, and he uses the title as though it had been given instead of collected. He's in the outer bailey, south-east of the mill, and he'll meet you in the open because he thinks of it as his ground. Bring the blade back when you're done. I'd like it to stop being his, and there's no one left alive it can be returned to.
hbe_stillwater.accept_text: He isn't entirely wrong about it being his ground. Make him wrong.
hbe_stillwater.turn_in_text:
It's grey beneath the violet, same as all of them.

I'll hang it up in Tarren Mill. It isn't a trophy. It's a reminder that this keep had a garrison once, and they lost it, and nobody came.

hbe_teague.description: Somebody else watches the wall. He's been at it thirty years by the state of his gear, on a stretch of stone no army has come near in living memory. He won't let anyone approach the gap, including anyone who might be going there to open it. Thirty years is a long time to practise not stepping back, and I've got four years on this wall and I already understand him, which worries me. He's at the gap, with a border pike long enough to keep Arathi on the far side of the stone.
hbe_teague.accept_text: He won't step back from that pike. Don't wait for him to.

hbe_the_gate.description: I hold the west end of the trunk road, and everything that reaches the east half of Hillsbrad passes me first. I've got it down to about four seconds, a look at the boots and a look at the eyes, whether a traveller's going to make the gate or be found on the verge. Go east along the trunk road to the mill square, where Magistrate Pell holds the gate. When you get there, mind the race. It's a cut channel, deep the whole way, with three bridges and no fourth, and the wheel gives people back about a week after they try the water.
hbe_the_gate.accept_text: People try the water about twice a year. Don't be this year's second.
hbe_the_gate.turn_in_text:
You made it. I had you as a maker. The boots were right, and you looked at the treeline instead of the road.

It took me four seconds. I'm rarely wrong, and I'd rather not start now.

hbe_thrall_cell.description: I'm a scholar in a garrison with no use for one, and my interest in Durnholde has nothing to do with the military. Thrall was held in that keep as a boy, by the man who raised him to fight in a pit, and a fair share of everything the Horde has since become started inside those walls. Go through the fallen archway into the courtyard and stand in the middle of it, that's the whole task. You weren't here for any of it, and you've no reason to care whose childhood happened in a ruin. But you can walk in there and come back out, and I can't, and I'd like someone to tell me what the ground feels like.
hbe_thrall_cell.accept_text: I'm aware how it sounds. Stand there long enough to notice something, then come back.

hbe_wall_watch.description: Thoradin's Wall was raised by Arathor, the first human empire, the one every kingdom since was carved out of, and it still closes the road into Arathi. I watch the near face, and I've never seen the far side or met anyone who has. Go south-east and walk the near face end to end. You'll have seen a lot of new things since you came to this world, but that wall was old when Lordaeron was founded. Everything you've watched fall this year was built in its shadow.
hbe_wall_watch.accept_text: Don't try the gap. There are ogres in it, and they've been there longer than I've been posted here.
hbe_wall_watch.turn_in_text:
So it's still shut.

An empire falls, then the kingdoms it made fall, and the wall outlives all of them without a garrison. There's a lesson in that, and I've never once enjoyed it.

hbe_worgs.description: I was gamekeeper on this land when it had a lord worth keeping game for. I know every hedgerow between the mill and the hollow, which is how I know that every one of them now has something living in it that didn't use to. Hunt the worg prowlers in the hedges between the road and the hollow. They run in threes, and that isn't a rule of thumb, it's how they're built. One shows itself, one circles, and one waits behind you.
hbe_worgs.accept_text: If you've found one, you've found three. Count to three before you swing.
hbe_worgs.turn_in_text:
And you counted before you swung. I could tell from how few of them got round you.

Most people don't. Most people learn on the second worg, if they get one.

hbw_arrows.description: I take a ram off the high pasture now and again, which the Marshal calls theft and I call older than the Marshal. My grandfather took rams off that hill when Alterac still had a king, and nobody's shown me the paper that changed it. What I can't do is make arrows fast enough to stay ahead of the wasps, the worgs and the patrols all at once. You've got hands, and there's a bench right there. Fletch me some batches of rough shafts, and we'll call the ram I owe you square.
hbw_arrows.accept_text: Count the feathers before you bind them. I'll be counting them after.
hbw_arrows.turn_in_text: That's my month. And you're a better fletcher than you are a liar. I watched you count the feathers.

hbw_calder.description: A farming valley with a Field Marshal is either a joke or a warning. Calder drills the militia in the barley with a real officer's sabre and a real officer's manner, and somewhere in the last month the farmhands stopped standing in a crowd and started standing in ranks. He drills them in open ground where anyone can see, which is arrogance, and he won't break and run, which isn't. I'd rather fight one officer than the hundred farmers he's six months from making. He'll be on the drill ground in the Hillsbrad Fields, south-east of this tower, in the middle of the valley.
hbw_calder.accept_text: That's the whole of my reasoning, and I'd say it to his face. Go and say it for me.
hbw_calder.turn_in_text:
He swore on the soil, they tell me. That's the oath the militia take here. There's no king left to swear to, so they swear to the ground.

The ground kept its half. It usually does.

hbw_drowned.description: I swam ashore from the Maiden's Grace and sat on the shingle all night, waiting for the rest of the crew. They did come up, over the following week, one at a time, with the tide. Not one of them came up as themselves. Put down the drowned castaways along the tideline, and some of them will have faces I know. Do it anyway, and when you come back, don't tell me which ones. I've spent a month deciding not to find out, and I'd like to keep the decision.
hbw_drowned.accept_text: Go at low tide. They're slower on dry shingle than they are in the shallows.

hbw_east_road.description: I've ridden the east road since Southpoint was taken, and I've got to the point of describing Tarren Mill from memory. Memory won't do for a report. The stretch past the Foothills is long enough that a lone rider stops being a courier and starts being an opportunity, so ride it east, the whole length. You'll know Tarren Mill when you see the wheel, a mill on a diverted race that cuts the town clean in two. That wheel's turned for sixty years, through the fall of Lordaeron and the Scourge and the valley changing hands twice. Report to Magistrate Pell at the gate.
hbw_east_road.accept_text: Keep moving past the Foothills, and don't stop for anyone waving at you from the hedges.

hbw_farmhands.description: My whole trade is knowing what a valley is doing before the valley announces it. This one is arming the people who bring in the barley, and calling it a harvest watch. Go after the farmhands out in the rows, but I don't want the count. I want to know what's in their hands when they go down. A billhook is a tool a frightened man picks up, and a halberd is a thing somebody made, carried to a field, and put into his hands on purpose. If you find halberds out there, this stopped being a harvest watch before either of us arrived.
hbw_farmhands.accept_text: Look at what they drop, not at them. The steel's the part that tells me something.
hbw_farmhands.turn_in_text:
Most of them had halberds.

Someone is arming this valley, and it isn't Southshore's garrison, because they'd keep the good steel for marines. That leaves a quartermaster with a grudge, or Alterac money. I'll find out.

hbw_green_country.description: Silverpine ends at a line you can see from this saddle, pine and blight on one side and barley on the other. Lordaeron fell and took its farmland with it, all but this valley. I've held this pass for two years, and every courier stops dead at the top of the road to look at the colour of it. I did too, the first time. I'd been two years dead, it was the first green I'd seen since, and I stood there like a fool. Go down and get it over with, because Commander Rethven holds the square tower with our banner, Southpoint, and she'll want to hear what the pass road looks like behind you.
hbw_green_country.accept_text: Stop and look if you need to. Everyone does, and I won't tell anybody.
hbw_green_country.turn_in_text: So you stopped. Don't apologise for it. The day I meet someone who walks past that view without pausing is the day I stop trusting my own eyes.

hbw_harlow.description: I burn da Southshore dock twice already. Both times it's standing again inside a month, and both times da man who fills da work gangs is a bosun called Harlow, who don't ask who wants da job. I burn da dock, dey build it, I burn it again, dey build it again. Dis time I take away da man who finds da hands. He works da approaches outside da town gate, south of here, signing up hands off da farms.
hbw_harlow.accept_text: He uses da blunderbuss first, so you close fast or you don't close at all.
hbw_harlow.turn_in_text: Hah, now dey rebuild it a third time! Dey do it slower, much slower, and dey pay more for it.

hbw_harpooner.description: The Daggerspine work the shallows with a barbed harpoon on a line, and the barb is the whole problem, because it doesn't come back out. Three of my watch have gone off the shingle in a month, and the line went with them each time. Whoever takes the first throw is fighting the rest of it anchored. Don't let it land, that's the only advice worth giving. He's at the north end of the strand, in the shallows where the shelf drops.
hbw_harpooner.accept_text: Close the distance or stay well off it. Anywhere in between is where the line finds you.
hbw_harpooner.turn_in_text: You cut the line rather than pull it, which is right. That's three men's worth of sense, and it only cost us the three men to learn it.

hbw_icehide.description: One yeti has used the same gully for eleven years. He's cost me lambs, two dogs, a fence and most of my patience, and he's old enough now to be white around the muzzle. I've driven him off four times, and he's never once run, which I've never been able to explain to anyone. He's in the top gully, where the stream comes out of the rock. I'd like this to be the last conversation about him.
hbw_icehide.accept_text: Take the cloak off the peg by the door before you go. It was my husband's, and it's seen that gully before.
hbw_icehide.turn_in_text:
That's eleven years, finished.

I thought I'd feel lighter. Keep the cloak. It's been up that hill twice now and come back down once with the business finished, and it's earned a better owner than a peg.

hbw_living_soil.description: For four years I've worked blighted earth, because blighted earth is what Tirisfal has. Then I crossed a ridge and found soil with roots in it. I haven't said so to the Commander, but I'm taking samples before anyone upriver decides green farmland is a problem that needs solving. I want jars of loam from several different fields, kept apart, because how they differ is the entire point. And since you aren't from here, tell me what soil smells like where you're from. I've been trying to remember what it's supposed to smell like, and I find I can't.
hbw_living_soil.accept_text: Don't fill them all from the nearest ditch. I'll know, and I'll be disappointed in you.
hbw_living_soil.turn_in_text:
They're living, all of them, roots, mites, the lot.

You said yours smelled like rain on stone. I'm going to think about that for a while.

hbw_militia.description: Twice a week, Hillsbrad's militia walk up the tower road, stand at a respectful distance, look at Southpoint, and walk away. My orders say hold the tower. They say nothing about men who come to count my walls and never once draw. They're farmers with billhooks and a grievance, and the grievance is fair, because we're standing in their valley. But men who've measured my gate for a month are deciding something, and I'd rather they decided it with fewer of them. Deal with the ones in the Hillsbrad Fields, south-east of this tower, where you'll see the fences from the road.
hbw_militia.accept_text: I've thought about this longer than it sounds. Go and do it, and don't enjoy it.

hbw_murlocs.description: I've counted the Daggerspine on the western strand for three weeks, and the count goes up every week. Murlocs don't breed that fast, which means they aren't breeding, they're arriving. They come up the beach facing inland, every one of them, so whatever they're running from is seaward. I've watched that water for three weeks, and it's never once looked back at me. Get them off the shingle for me.
hbw_murlocs.accept_text: While you're down there, keep half an eye on the water behind them.

hbw_ram_horns.description: Southpoint's glue, lamp oil, buttons and bowstring nocks all come off the same animal. I could requisition them through the Undercity, and the requisition would come back in the spring, correctly stamped, for half what I asked. Understand what you're doing for me, then. I can write to Lordaeron and be answered in April, or I can send you up a hill. The Dark Lady gave us our freedom, and nobody thought to give us a supply line. Bring me horns off the foothill rams, and I'll have oil in the lamps by Thursday.
hbw_ram_horns.accept_text: Matched pairs if you can manage it. I sign for everything twice, and odd horns make the ledger sulk.

hbw_signet.description: You turn the ring over in your palm. It's a good signet, silver, and it's been in salt water long enough that the finger it came off swelled around it before anything let go. The crest is a ship under three stars, a merchantman's mark, not a navy's. Someone on this coast will know it, and will wish they didn't. There's a woman camped above the tideline on Purgation Shore who came ashore off a wreck and never went inland.
hbw_signet.accept_text: Start with the woman above the tideline on Purgation Shore.
hbw_signet.turn_in_text:
A ship under three stars.

That's the Maiden's Grace. That's my ship, and that's Harl's hand it came off, because he was the only one of us with fingers fat enough to need it cut.

Keep it, please. I've looked at that water for a month, and I don't need something to hold while I do it.

hbw_southshore_watch.description: I've watched Southshore from the treeline for a year and never once walked into it. It's one of the last living human towns left standing in the north, it knows it, and it has three hundred marines who know it too. Walk in through the gate at the end of the trunk road, south of here, like you've got business there, and go straight down the high street to the quay. They don't start fights on their own street, but they'll watch every step you take. I want the dock, and I want to know how many hulls are tied up at it. Be clear with yourself before you go, because if they take you, nobody's coming.
hbw_southshore_watch.accept_text: Go unarmed and look poor. Keep your hands where they can see them.
hbw_southshore_watch.turn_in_text:
How many hulls was it? As many as that?

Then we aren't taking Southshore this year, nor next. I'll send that north, and someone in the Undercity will be disappointed in a way that doesn't reach us, which suits me.

hbw_thistlewing.description: A hive this size has a queen, and she's why the orchard has wasps the size of a hand instead of wasps the size of wasps. She's taken the old cider press at the orchard's heart and built into it. My father pressed in that building. I'd rather have it back than be sensible about this. She's in the press house, dead centre of the rows.
hbw_thistlewing.accept_text: Her sting puts a grown man down for a slow count of ten. Don't be standing anywhere stupid when it lands.
hbw_thistlewing.turn_in_text: The hive'll scatter inside the week. There'll be cider by autumn, and the first barrel's yours, and I won't hear otherwise.

hbw_tidewrack.description: Something's holding the Maiden's Grace on the bottom. I've seen it twice from the shingle, a mass of anchor chain, spar and hull moving under its own weight. It drags what's left of my ship further out with every tide. It isn't a ghost and it isn't a beast, it's wreckage that got given a purpose by something, and it's been collecting my ship a piece at a time for a month. Go at high water, at the south end, and take the purpose out of it.
hbw_tidewrack.accept_text: You'll hear the chain before you see it.

hbw_wasps.description: The Hillsbrad orchard still fruits, which after the last five years is very close to a miracle. The wasps that have taken it are the size of a man's hand. Every orchard between here and Lordaeron is ash or worse, and this one came through. I'm not losing it to insects after it survived the end of a kingdom. I'd like the apples, and I'd also like to keep my face, so go in among the rows for me.
hbw_wasps.accept_text: Keep your chin tucked. They go for the eyes, and they're clever about it.

hbw_worgs.description: Worgs on the pass road are ordinary. Worgs that work the same stretch at the same hour aren't. I've lost two couriers in a month, both on the run between the pass and the tower, both within an hour of dusk, and I've stopped calling it bad luck. They hunt the verges, so take the crown of the road and make them come out to you. While you're at it, mark where they've been bedding, because a worg that beds within sight of a road has stopped being a wolf and become a picket. Pickets get posted by something.
hbw_worgs.accept_text: I'm not standing here counting for you. Come back when the road's quiet, and tell me where they slept.

hbw_yeti.description: I've read weather off my animals for thirty years. My rams have been bunching at the low fence for a week and refusing the top pasture, which means the yetis have come down early. That means the snowline's moved, and the winter's going to be a bad one. I'll say this plain, because I've been told what you are: you get back up, so you can walk a gully I'd not send my own son up. I'd be a liar if I said that didn't sit strange with me. Take the work anyway, up where the grass goes thin, because I need the pasture more than I need to be comfortable about it.
hbw_yeti.accept_text: Go in daylight. They're slow in the sun, and you'll see them before they see you.

tm_apothecary_reagents.description: My vats run on things that have to be gathered instead of bought, and the Mudsnout gnolls have taken the hollow where most of them grow. I'd rather send someone than explain to the Society why a quarter's work stalled over fungus. Bring me bloodcaps out of the wet ground in Mudsnout Hollow, where the water sits. Cut them, don't pull them, because the whole value's in the stem. And don't eat one on a dare, because I've had that conversation twice, and one of those people is still here, after a fashion.
tm_apothecary_reagents.accept_text: Wrap the stems in something damp. They bruise on the walk back if you don't.
tm_apothecary_reagents.turn_in_text:
They're cut clean. That's a quarter's work secured, and one fewer letter I've got to write.

Mind the vats on your way out. What's in them isn't finished, and it doesn't like being looked at.

tm_apprentice_jars.description: I label every jar in the apothecarium, and it isn't the junior work it sounds like. A consignment came in from Gavin's Naze last month with half the labels soaked off in transit, and some unmarked jars went back out with it before anyone noticed. Nobody in this building will open an unmarked jar to find out what's in it. The whole discipline is that you know what you're holding. An unlabelled jar in a Syndicate camp is somebody's accident waiting to be somebody else's epidemic. Bring them back to me from the Naze, closed.
tm_apprentice_jars.accept_text: If the wax is broken on one, leave it alone and tell me.

tm_bowyer_yew.description: I string bows the way my father strung them, which means yew off the river stand and nothing else. My father cut there, and his father, and there's a mark on one of those trunks that's four generations of us deep. Now the gnolls have been felling the river stand for den stakes. They're burning four generations of it to hold up their roofs. Take the staves back off them, three miles out past the hedgerows.
tm_bowyer_yew.accept_text: Look at the cut before you pick one up. I want heartwood and sapwood both, or it's firewood.

tm_chaplain.description: I keep a chapel on the west bank, a living chaplain in a town held by the Forsaken, and nobody's ever told me to stop. I bury the village's dead in ground the Society could want, and so far nobody's wanted it. Markers have gone missing out of the yard, stone ones with names cut in them, most likely to the Syndicate, because cut stone sells. I'll say the thing nobody here says to you. You die and you get up again, and the people in my yard don't, so you'll understand why a man in my trade thinks about it when you walk past. Bring the markers home.
tm_chaplain.accept_text: I've no quarrel with you for what you are. I only want the names back where they were put.
tm_chaplain.turn_in_text:
The names are back in the ground where they were put.

That's all a marker is, a promise that somebody stays where they were laid. It's the only promise I've got left to keep, and I'd rather keep it.

tm_commander_syndicate.description: I hold the middle of a valley with Alterac at my back and Southshore at my front, and of the two, I lose more sleep over Alterac. Southshore is a garrison and behaves like one. Alterac let the Horde through the pass in the Second War, and the Alliance dissolved the kingdom for it. The lords went into these hills with their titles and no land, a court in exile with money, grudges and fifteen years of practice, and courts in exile want their country back. Go after their Syndicate spellbinders wherever you find them east of the mill.
tm_commander_syndicate.accept_text: Take the binders first. A court can always find another son, but not another wizard so easily.
tm_commander_syndicate.turn_in_text: They'll replace them. A court always has another son. But it buys me a season, and a season in this valley is a long time.

tm_farrier.description: I keep half this town moving, hooves and hinges. The caravan runs west twice a month, and the last runs came back with the draught team lame. I traced it to shoes cut from the cheap bronze stock the Society bought in bulk. Make me sets of heavy bronze plate at the forge, and I'll cut the shoe stock off them myself, because plate's the right thickness and their bar stock isn't. I know it's a strange way round, but I'd rather ruin good plate than put another team lame on the west road.
tm_farrier.accept_text: Heavy plate, properly tempered. Bring them to me before anyone tries them on.

tm_innkeeper_pot.description: I feed both banks, which is a diplomatic position I never asked for, and I handle it by not asking anybody which side they came off. The trouble is that half my custom eats and the other half watches, and the half that eats has opinions about mutton. I want good haunches off the foothill rams, west past the Foothills. I mean ram, mind, not sheep, because this room can taste the difference and will tell me about it for a week. Take the west road, not the hollow, because I've lost two suppliers to that hollow already.
tm_innkeeper_pot.accept_text: Hang them properly on the way back if you've got time. I'll know if you didn't.

tm_miller_bands.description: My family's milled here sixty years. In that time Lordaeron fell, the valley changed hands twice, and the dead took the east bank, and the wheel hasn't stopped for any of it. My grandfather kept it going through the Second War by swapping the bands out himself. The spindle bands have started to go now, and you can't improvise a spindle band. I want bars of iron, smelted properly, and I wouldn't like to be the Reed who let her stop over a few bars.
tm_miller_bands.accept_text: Iron, not bronze. I know what bronze does in a wet bearing, and so will you after one winter.

tm_scout_keep.description: I walk the roads so the garrison doesn't have to guess. Durnholde's the one place I've never been able to report on properly, because the Syndicate hold the walls and I've only ever seen the keep from the bluff. It's a ring, outer wall, inner keep, and a courtyard between them. If the inner keep's still sealed, they're holding it properly and we need a plan, and if it's open, they're squatting and we need a day. Go through the fallen archway into the gatehouse ground and look.
tm_scout_keep.accept_text: Go far enough to count what's standing, and not far enough to be counted yourself.
tm_scout_keep.turn_in_text:
It's sealed, of course it's sealed.

They've been in there fifteen years, and they've kept the inner keep shut the whole time. People squatting don't do that. That's a garrison, and I'll report it as one.

tm_sluice.description: My crank raises the sluice. Drop the gate, and the wheel stops, the mill stops, the Society's vats go cold, and every person on both banks remembers my name within the hour. For a week the race has been running slow, and something's choking the intake above the weir that isn't weed. I've been doing this twenty-two years, and I know what weed feels like on the rake. I'd rather be the man who asked than the man who dropped the gate on a guess. Bring me whatever you pull out of the grating.
tm_sluice.accept_text: Use the rake by the weir, and keep your hands out of the grating itself.

tm_smith_charcoal.description: I shoe the Society's horses, mend their cart axles and take their money, and I've stopped apologising for it to anyone who asks. A trade's a trade. What I won't do is burn the coal they keep sending from Dun Garok's old workings, because it's cheaper and hotter and it ruins a weld. You get a seam that looks perfect and opens in a year, and I won't put my mark on that. Bring me oakheart planks, cut and seasoned at a sawmill, and I'll burn my own charcoal.
tm_smith_charcoal.accept_text: It has to be seasoned. Green wood spits, and I can tell by the weight before I've split one.

tm_stable_worgs.description: My horses won't cross the bridges after dark. I've tried leading them, blindfolding them and bribing them. They cross all day without complaint and refuse from dusk, and the only thing that's changed is the number of worgs working the hedgerows on the far side. Horses don't reason it out, they just know, and they're right more often than the men leading them. Clear the worgs out of the hedges east of the race, and I'll try the bridge at dusk again.
tm_stable_worgs.accept_text: Go at dusk if you can. That's when they're out, and that's when my horses can smell them.

tm_two_banks.description: I've got the south gate, which means I give the same speech eight or nine times a day, and I've pared it down to its working parts. The town's cut in half by a millrace. The west bank's the old village, with the inn, the forge, the chapel and the mill, and the east bank's the Royal Apothecary Society and their vats. Three bridges join them, there's no fourth, the water's deep the whole way, and the wheel doesn't care who you were. Walk north from this gate to the market bridge in the Mill Yard, and look at both banks before you do anything else.
tm_two_banks.accept_text: That's the whole errand, and it saves me a conversation later.

tm_vat_tender.description: I tend the vats on the east bank, and it's the best thing that's happened to me since dying. The work needs a reagent the Society gets from Durnholde's undercroft. They used to send a cart there twice a year and nobody minded, and now there are wizards on the gate. I've been dead twelve years and I've got a trade again, stir it, skim it, log it, and I'm not losing it because Alterac's leftovers found religion. Go after their Syndicate spellbinders, inside the keep.
tm_vat_tender.accept_text: Clear the gate, and the cart can go out again.
